classification.difficultyReason: Combine a similarity proof and proportion with a changed geometric model, then equate complementary areas and select an exact positive length.

content.prompt: A triangular region of land ($\triangle ACD$) is divided up into two areas, Block 1 and Block 2, to make way for residential development. Details regarding the plan are provided in the given diagram.

spec.description: Triangle ACD rises from A to D. B lies on AC and E on AD, with BE perpendicular to AC. Block labels, Street, both right-angle marks and double-headed measurement arrows are retained. Ordinary source blue geometry is rendered in house black; no fill is needed.
spec.mathematics: AB:BC=20:10, BE=20 m, BC=10 m and CD=30 m. A, B, C are collinear; A, E, D are collinear.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and labels are visible; no calculated length or area is supplied.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that $\triangle ABE$ is similar to $\triangle ACD$.

answer.short: $\triangle ABE\sim\triangle ACD$ (AAA): $\angle ABE=\angle ACD=90^\circ$ and $\angle BAE=\angle CAD$.
answer.worked: $\angle ABE=\angle ACD=90^\circ$ (given), and $\angle BAE=\angle CAD$ (common angle at $A$). The third pair of angles is therefore equal. Hence $\triangle ABE\sim\triangle ACD$ by AAA, with corresponding vertices $A\leftrightarrow A$, $B\leftrightarrow C$ and $E\leftrightarrow D$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: By letting $AB=x$ metres, write, in terms of $x$:

children.label: ii
children.prompt: an equation linking $x$ with the lengths $EB$, $AC$ and $CD$

answer.worked:
Matching sides of the similar triangles give:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AB}{AC}&=\frac{EB}{CD}\\\frac{x}{x+10}&=\frac{20}{30}\\\frac{x}{x+10}&=\frac{2}{3}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Solve the equation in part b ii to find the length $AB$.

inlines.text: The subdivider now considers moving the position of the fence

answer.worked:
Here $AB=BE=x\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of Block 1}&=\frac12\times AB\times BE\\\text{Area of Block 1}&=\frac12\times x\times x\\\text{Area of Block 1}&=\frac12x^2\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of }\triangle ACD&=\frac12\times30\times30\\\text{Area of }\triangle ACD&=450\text{ m}^2\\\text{Area of Block 2}&=\text{Area of }\triangle ACD-\text{Area of Block 1}\\\text{Area of Block 2}&=\left(450-\frac12x^2\right)\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: If the subdivider requires that the area of Block 1 is to be the same as the area of Block 2:

children.label: i
children.prompt: write an equation in $x$ to represent this situation

answer.worked:
Equating the areas of the two blocks gives
$$\frac12x^2=450-\frac12x^2.$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: find the length $AB$ ($x$ metres) as a surd in simplest form

answer.short:
$AB=15\sqrt2\text{ m}$

Equate the two areas and take the positive square root.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac12x^2&=450-\frac12x^2\\x^2&=450\\x&=\sqrt{450}\\x&=\sqrt{225\times2}\\x&=15\sqrt2\end{align*}$$
Take the positive root because $x$ is a length. Hence $AB=15\sqrt2\text{ m}$, which lies between $0$ and $30\text{ m}$ as required.
